review_flags.wl35_two_products_one_video: Video names two compounded products; it was gated as both tirzepatide and semaglutide. Each needs compounded sign-off.
review_flags.wl35_illustrative_vials: Vials are 3D illustrations (glass, liquid, cap, a blank paper band with two honey stripes, no text). They are not the real Beema Health/pharmacy vial or label and are labeled 'Illustration' on screen. Matt to confirm this is acceptable versus the live-site vial renders (which carry 'Weight loss Medication' and a syringe).
review_flags.wl35_generic_shipping_box: The pharmacy packaging scene is a generic plain kraft box with a white insulated pouch and honey tape. It is not the real pharmacy/Bask packaging. Confirm or supply a real packaging photo.
review_flags.wl35_independent_evaluation_wording: Brief said 'independent clinical evaluation'. Script says 'a clinical evaluation' because 'independent' (providers independent of Beema Health/Bask?) is unverified. Matt decides.
review_flags.wl35_notice_vs_spoken_disclosure: The brief's notice is on screen from the first product mention through the end card, and a shortened disclosure is SPOKEN in the closing line. The standard engine closing line ('Prescription required. Prescribing is never guaranteed, and you won't be charged if you aren't prescribed') is NOT spoken (time budget); the no-charge line is on the end card only. Matt decides whether that satisfies the gate.
review_flags.wl35_no_word_captions: This Story uses kinetic headlines that mirror the narration instead of word-by-word captions. Confirm that is acceptable for accessibility (IG auto-captions can be enabled).
review_flags.wl35_waiting_room_metaphor: Hook shows empty waiting-room chairs leaving. Implies convenience, not an outcome. Confirm no comparison claim against in-person clinics is read into it.
